info.title: operator-gateway
info.summary: Anti-corruption layer that turns a bespoke client's operator actions into edge-api calls.
info.description:
A client's Node-RED tee posts operator actions (downtime justification/edit, PO start/stop/setup/replace/status/time, event split) here. For every action the gateway: requires POST (405 otherwise), checks `X-Ingest-Key` (401), decodes the JSON body (400; unknown fields are allowed), checks the tenant scope (403), resolves `packml_topic` to the tenant's equipment via `packml_register` (422 when it does not resolve, 503 on DB failure), maps the request to the edge-api DTO (422 when a required field is missing), and forwards it to edge-api with the gateway's own edge-api key.

Tenant scope: one enterprise per instance (INCOPLAST_ENTERPRISE_ID, INCOPLAST_TOPIC_PREFIX). A request passes only if it positively matches: `enterprise` equals the configured id, or the topic starts with the configured prefix; a mismatch on either is rejected. The tenant is never chosen by the caller: edge-api is always called with the configured enterprise id.

Server-side resolution: `id_equipment`, `id_site`, `id_area` and `cd_machine` always come from the resolved topic (active register rows of the configured enterprise only; exactly one match required); values supplied in the body are ignored. Resolutions are cached in-process for 5 minutes (misses for 30 seconds), so a newly activated topic can 422 for up to 30 s and a deactivated one keeps resolving for up to 5 min.

Result translation: edge-api 2xx -> 202 `{"status":"accepted"}`; edge-api 4xx -> the same status and edge-api's body passed through; edge-api 5xx -> 502; edge-api unreachable or slower than 10 s -> 503.

Idempotency: the gateway adds none. Creates (downtime justify/manual, PO create-and-start, setup with `should_create_po`) are not safe to replay blindly: a 503 `edge-api unreachable` caused by the 10 s timeout, or a 502, can follow a write edge-api already committed. 503 `topic resolver unavailable` is always safe to retry (nothing was sent).

Transport: TLS-only listener (PORT default 8443; cert/key from TLS_CERT_FILE/TLS_KEY_FILE). Public exposure: none. No nginx vhost routes to this service (the `operator.<domain>` vhosts serve the operator SPA, a different container). Staging publishes 127.0.0.1:8445 -> 8443 on the host loopback only. Production defines it behind the `client-ingest` compose profile and publishes 8445 on all host interfaces, but the production security group does not admit 8445. The servers below are in-network addresses.

Ops routes not described here: `/healthz` (503 when the resolver DB pool is unreachable) and `/metrics` (Prometheus).

## How to call this API

- **Auth**: send the shared tee key in the `X-Ingest-Key` header on every request (no Bearer, no query-string key). The key is per deployment (server env OPERATOR_API_KEY); ask the platform team for it and keep it out of logs.
- **Base URLs**: see `servers`. Both are in-network only (packiot-net or the host loopback); there is no public URL. TLS with the stack's internal certificate (`curl -k` from the host).
- **Content types**: request `application/json` (UTF-8), one action object per request, at most 1 MiB. Every response is `application/json`. Method is always POST.
- **Errors**: the gateway's own errors are `{"error":"<message>"}` (Go json.Encoder, trailing newline). edge-api 4xx responses are passed through with edge-api's own body (NestJS shape `{"statusCode":..,"message":..,"error":..}`), so check the shape before parsing. Statuses: 400 bad JSON, 401 bad key, 403 out of tenant scope, 405 not POST, 422 unresolvable topic or missing field (do not retry unchanged), 502/503 retryable with care (see Idempotency).
- **Docs**: browse this spec in the API docs portal https://api.staging.packiot.app/docs/ (cs-admin SSO, read-only Swagger UI). The spec is also exported to `docs/api/openapi/operator-gateway.openapi.json` in packiot-stack-alpha.

servers.description: In-network on packiot-net (alias operator-adapter). Staging static IP 172.18.0.30:8443; production 172.18.0.31:8443.
Local development / staging host loopback publish (127.0.0.1:8445 -> 8443)

tags.name: downtime
tags.description: Stop reasons from the operator: justify a detected stop, register a manual event, edit/trim an event, or split it into re-categorised parts.

tags.name: production-orders
tags.description: Production-order lifecycle from the operator: create+start, stop (pause/finish), setup (close + open next), replace, toggle status, edit runtime interval times.

post.summary: Justify, register or edit a downtime event
post.description:
Records the operator's reason for a stop. Routed on `id_param` (the SparkPlug Parameter id the client's flow assigns):

| id_param | Meaning | edge-api call |
|---|---|---|
| 30810 | justify a detected stop | `POST /api/downtimes/create-manual-event` |
| 30811 | new manual event | `POST /api/downtimes/create-manual-event` |
| 30812 | change an existing event | `POST /api/downtimes/edit-manual-event` (needs `id_equipment_event`) |
| 30813, 30814 | trim an existing event's end | `POST /api/downtimes/edit-manual-event` (needs `id_equipment_event`) |

`category`, `category_desc`, `ts_event`, `ts_end` are always required. `planned_dwt`, `change_over` and `idle` are sent on the edit path only (the create DTO has no columns for them; they are ignored there). `cd_machine` and `id_equipment` come from the resolved topic (an equipment with a NULL `cd_equipment` yields 422 `cd_machine is required ...`).

Side effects: edge-api writes the downtime event row (equipment_events) and an audit row in user_logs. Not idempotent at the gateway: retrying a create after a timeout can create a second event.

Order of checks (each step fails closed): POST only (405) → `X-Ingest-Key` (401) → JSON decode, 1 MiB cap, unknown fields ignored (400) → tenant scope (403) → SparkPlug topic → equipment resolution (422 unresolved, 503 resolver DB error) → field mapping to the edge-api DTO (422, message names the field) → POST to edge-api with the gateway's own key and `?idEnterprise=<configured id>` (2xx → 202, 4xx → passed through, other → 502, transport error/timeout → 503).

requestBody.description: One operator action. Tenant envelope fields plus the action fields; extra Node-RED metadata keys are accepted and ignored.

400.description: `invalid JSON body`: malformed JSON, a wrongly typed field (e.g. a string where an integer is expected, an `id_order` that is neither string nor number), or a body over 1 MiB. Also returned verbatim when edge-api itself answers 400 (validation), with edge-api's body.

401.description: `invalid or missing X-Ingest-Key` (also when the server has no key configured). A 401 with an edge-api-shaped body instead means edge-api rejected the gateway's own EDGE_API_KEY (server misconfiguration, not your key).

403.description: The body's `enterprise` / SparkPlug topic do not positively match the instance's configured tenant (or neither is present). A 403 with an edge-api-shaped body is edge-api's own refusal, passed through.

422.description: Fail-closed rejection, never retried successfully without changing the body: the SparkPlug topic is empty, does not resolve to exactly one active equipment of this tenant, or a required field for edge-api `/api/downtimes/create-manual-event | /api/downtimes/edit-manual-event` is missing/invalid. The message names the field. (Unlikely but possible: edge-api's own 422, passed through.)

post.summary: Create and start a production order
post.description:
Creates a production order for the resolved equipment and starts it (edge-api `POST /api/production-orders/create-and-start`). The order number (`id_order`) is the client's number, kept as text exactly as sent (ADR-0062) and forwarded in both `idOrder` and `orderNumber`; `id_site`, `id_area`, `id_equipment` come from the resolved topic. Required: `id_order`, `production_order_quantity`, `timestamp`.

Side effects: edge-api inserts the production order and its first runtime interval and writes a user_logs audit row. Not idempotent at the gateway: a retry after a timeout may create a duplicate PO; check before retrying.

Order of checks (each step fails closed): POST only (405) → `X-Ingest-Key` (401) → JSON decode, 1 MiB cap, unknown fields ignored (400) → tenant scope (403) → SparkPlug topic → equipment resolution (422 unresolved, 503 resolver DB error) → field mapping to the edge-api DTO (422, message names the field) → POST to edge-api with the gateway's own key and `?idEnterprise=<configured id>` (2xx → 202, 4xx → passed through, other → 502, transport error/timeout → 503).

post.summary: Pause or finish the running production order
post.description:
Stops the running PO on the resolved equipment (edge-api `POST /api/production-orders/stop`, audit eventType `order-stopped`). `stop_type` accepts `pause`/`interrupt`/`1` (→ `pause`) or `finish`/`2` (→ `finish`), case-insensitive. `production_order_quantity` is the final good count edge-api stores on the PO.

Side effects: edge-api updates the PO status and closes its runtime interval; user_logs audit row. Repeating the call depends on edge-api's state checks (a second stop of an already-stopped PO is edge-api's call, typically a 4xx).

Order of checks (each step fails closed): POST only (405) → `X-Ingest-Key` (401) → JSON decode, 1 MiB cap, unknown fields ignored (400) → tenant scope (403) → SparkPlug topic → equipment resolution (422 unresolved, 503 resolver DB error) → field mapping to the edge-api DTO (422, message names the field) → POST to edge-api with the gateway's own key and `?idEnterprise=<configured id>` (2xx → 202, 4xx → passed through, other → 502, transport error/timeout → 503).

post.summary: Close the current production order, optionally open next
post.description:
Atomic "close the current PO and optionally open the next" (edge-api `POST /api/production-orders/setup`, eventType `order-changed`). Variants:

- `should_open_new_po=false` → close only.
- `should_open_new_po=true`, `should_create_po=true` → create a new PO from `id_order` (+ `production_order_quantity`, `nm_production_order`, `notes`, `id_label`) and start it.
- `should_open_new_po=true`, `should_create_po` false/absent → start the existing PO `id_production_order`.

Absent optional integers are sent to edge-api as 0 and absent booleans as false. Side effects: PO status/runtime rows for both POs; user_logs audit row. Not idempotent.

Order of checks (each step fails closed): POST only (405) → `X-Ingest-Key` (401) → JSON decode, 1 MiB cap, unknown fields ignored (400) → tenant scope (403) → SparkPlug topic → equipment resolution (422 unresolved, 503 resolver DB error) → field mapping to the edge-api DTO (422, message names the field) → POST to edge-api with the gateway's own key and `?idEnterprise=<configured id>` (2xx → 202, 4xx → passed through, other → 502, transport error/timeout → 503).

post.description:

post.summary: Edit a production-order runtime interval's start and end
post.description:
Rewrites the bounds of runtime interval `id_production_order_runtime` of PO `id_production_order` (edge-api `POST /api/production-orders/change-time`, eventType `order-time-changed`). `end` is optional (empty string forwarded as-is). Setting the same bounds again is idempotent in effect. Side effects: production_orders_runtime row; OEE for the touched window is recomputed downstream; user_logs audit row.

post.summary: Split one event into re-categorised sub-intervals
post.description:
Splits event `id_equipment_event` into the given sub-intervals, each with its own category (edge-api `POST /api/downtimes/split`, eventType `event-splitted`). Every sub-interval's `machineCode` is the resolved `cd_machine`. Per sub-interval `start_time`, `category_code`, `desc_category`, `idle` (Yes|yes|No|no), `change_over` and `planned_dwt` are required; `event_type` must be downtime|manual|low_speed. Distinct from the trim path of POST /operator/downtime.

Side effects: edge-api replaces the original event with the sub-events; user_logs audit row. Not idempotent (the original event no longer exists after a successful split).

Order of checks (each step fails closed): POST only (405) → `X-Ingest-Key` (401) → JSON decode, 1 MiB cap, unknown fields ignored (400) → tenant scope (403) → SparkPlug topic → equipment resolution (422 unresolved, 503 resolver DB error) → field mapping to the edge-api DTO (422, message names the field) → POST to edge-api with the gateway's own key and `?idEnterprise=<configured id>` (2xx → 202, 4xx → passed through, other → 502, transport error/timeout → 503).

ingestKey.name: X-Ingest-Key
ingestKey.description: Shared key for the client's tee node (OPERATOR_API_KEY), compared in constant time. An unset key on the server denies every request.

Accepted.description: edge-api accepted the call (any 2xx). The write has landed; nothing is queued.

MethodNotAllowed.description: `method not allowed`: only POST is accepted (no Allow header is set).

EdgePassthrough.description: Any other 4xx from edge-api (e.g. 404 unknown PO, 409 state conflict): edge-api's status code and body returned unchanged, with Content-Type forced to application/json. Do not retry unchanged.

EdgeBadGateway.description: `edge-api error`: edge-api answered 5xx (or any status outside 2xx/4xx). The write may or may not have happened; check before retrying a create.

Unavailable.description: Retryable infrastructure failure: `edge-api unreachable` (connect error, 10 s timeout or unreadable response; after a timeout edge-api MAY have committed the write), `topic resolver unavailable` (DB error; nothing was sent to edge-api) or `topic resolver is not configured`.

Error.description: Gateway error body. Written with Go's json.Encoder, so the body ends with a newline.

error.description: Human-readable reason; stable strings listed per response.

EdgeError.description: edge-api's own error body, passed through byte-for-byte (NestJS shape; defined by edge-api, not by this gateway).

message.description: Reason: a string or an array of validation messages.

OrderNumber.description: Client production-order number (ADR-0062): kept as text exactly as given, only surrounding whitespace trimmed. A JSON number keeps its literal text (834.058 → "834.058", no rounding). null, absent or blank means not supplied. Booleans/objects/arrays are a 400.

OperatorScope.description: Tenant envelope carried by every action. Unknown fields (Node-RED metadata such as socketid) are allowed and ignored. Scope passes only on a positive match: `enterprise` equals the configured id, or `packml_topic` starts with the configured topic prefix; a present-but-mismatching value on either rejects (403).

enterprise.description: Tenant id; must equal the instance's configured enterprise id when present.

topic.description: The operator app's user topic; carried for audit/debug, not used for scope or resolution.

packml_topic.description: SparkPlug topic of the equipment (required in practice: 422 when empty). Resolved server-side to id_equipment / id_area / id_site / cd_machine via the active `packml_register` rows of this tenant, and scope-checked against the configured prefix. Resolutions are cached 5 min (misses 30 s).

user.description: Operator id; audit only, never forwarded to edge-api or logged.

id_param.description: SparkPlug Parameter id selecting the path: 30810/30811 create, 30812/30813/30814 edit.

id_equipment_event.description: Event to edit; required for 30812-30814, ignored on create.

planned_dwt.description: Planned downtime flag; edit path only (absent = false).

change_over.description: Changeover flag; edit path only (absent = false).

idle.description: Idle marker forwarded verbatim; edit path only.

POStopRequest.description: Pause or finish the running PO.

timestamp.description: Stop time, ISO 8601 or `YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss` (forwarded verbatim).

id_production_order.description: Internal id of the running PO.

POSetupRequest.description: Close current PO, optionally open the next.

should_open_new_po.description: true = close current and open next; false = close only.

stop_type.description: How the current PO is closed: `pause`/`interrupt`/`1` or `finish`/`2`.

old_production_order_prod_final.description: Final good count of the PO being closed.

should_create_po.description: When opening next: true = create a new PO from `id_order`; false/absent = reuse `id_production_order`.

id_order.description: New PO's client order number; required when creating.

id_production_order.description: Existing next PO; required when opening without creating.

production_order_quantity.description: Programmed quantity of the new PO (absent = 0).

id_label.description: Label id for the new PO; optional.

id_production_order.description: PO whose paused/finished status is toggled.

SplitRequest.description: Split one event into re-categorised sub-intervals.

SplitEvent.description: One sub-interval. `machineCode` is filled server-side from the resolved equipment.

idle.description: Idle marker; exactly one of Yes, yes, No, no.

change_over.description: Changeover flag (required, false is a value).
